## Scope

A four-dimension cybersecurity training program (general awareness,
role-based, secure delivery, IR/DR) for a GCC Moderate boundary, with
machine-readable completion evidence exported to the governance substrate.
Thesis: **training is the one KSI that cannot be closed by architecture
alone** — it requires a human participation record, made continuously
demonstrable via LMS export, to activate KSI-CED-RAT and complete all 29
CR26 KSIs.

## Learning objectives

- Describe the four training dimensions KSI-CED-RAT evaluates and map each
  to its NIST control and evidence type.
- Design an AT-2 general awareness program (8 required modules) and select
  a GCC Moderate delivery platform.
- Build an AT-3 role-based training matrix across the six role tiers with
  frequencies and hour targets.
- Configure quarterly phishing simulation (AT-2(1)) with click-rate
  tracking and remedial-training triggers.
- Produce the `training-effectiveness-record` JSON and automate its
  monthly Viva Learning Graph API export.
- Plan the CP-3 quarterly tabletop calendar and IR-2 drill cadence,
  including after-action reports.
- State the PASS thresholds that flipped KSI-022 from scaffold to active.

## Key concepts

- The KSI-CED-RAT four-dimension model ("persistently reviews" training).
- Six-tier AT-3 role matrix: sysadmins, privileged users, developers,
  IR responders, data stewards, executives.
- `governance.training-effectiveness-record` JSON schema — the KSI-022
  evidence contract.
- Viva Learning Graph API export (`learningCourseActivities`,
  `LearningAssignmentReport.Read.All`).
- Delivery-platform trade-space: Viva Learning, DoD Cyber Awareness
  Challenge, CISA materials, KnowBe4/Proofpoint, SANS.
- IR scenario library (five minimum GCC Moderate scenarios); CP-3 Q1–Q4
  tabletop calendar.
- ≥95% completion thresholds per dimension/tier for PASS.

## Implementation sequence

1. Phase 1 (weeks 1–4): designate owner, select LMS, assign role tiers,
   configure the Graph API export, enroll all staff.
2. Phase 2 (weeks 5–12): launch the AT-2 campaign; launch Tier 1/Tier 3
   tracks; run the first phishing simulation and the SBOM/Grype developer
   lab; schedule the IR drill.
3. Phase 3 (weeks 13–16): deploy the monthly export Logic App; map to the
   JSON schema; ingest; validate KSI-022 PASS; archive the first
   after-action report.
4. Phase 4 (ongoing): monthly exports, quarterly phishing campaigns,
   semi-annual IR drills, annual tabletop calendar and content refresh,
   quarterly ISSO dashboard review.

## Compliance hooks

Closes 9 controls: AT-2, AT-2(1), AT-2(2), AT-3, AT-3(3), AT-3(5), AT-4,
CP-3, IR-2; SA-16 for secure delivery. FedRAMP 20x: KSI-CED-RAT
(KSI-022, "Reviewing All Training") — the final scaffold KSI, taking CR26
coverage to 29/29. NIST SP 800-50, SP 800-16; EO 14028; EO 13587;
OMB M-22-09.

## Prerequisites

Book 13 (Sentinel playbooks for IR-2), Book 14 (CP-2 plan and DR runbooks
for CP-3), Book 15 (Syft/Grype/VEX pipeline for developer training),
Book 16 (PM-14 plan, RACI), Book 17 (PT family for AT-3(5) PII training);
the Tier 1 curriculum spans Books 01–11.

## Labs

1. Generate a CycloneDX SBOM with Syft, triage a Grype scan, and write VEX
   assertions — the book's own Tier 3 developer lab.
2. Build the Graph API PowerShell export and transform the output into the
   `training-effectiveness-record` schema; validate the PASS logic.
3. Run a phishing → credential theft → lateral movement tabletop from the
   IR scenario library, with an after-action write-up.

## Pitfalls the book calls out

- A one-time training event satisfies nothing — KSI-CED-RAT demands
  persistent, machine-readable review.
- Aggregate-only phishing statistics fail AT-4; results must tie to user
  identity.
- Lecture-based developer training is ineffective — the pipeline gets
  treated as a compliance hurdle instead of a partner.
- Data stewards who don't understand DLP policy intent will attempt
  workarounds.
